cited_evidence: In job_1 assemble_provenance, the emitted evidence record uses "record_id": record.get('source_id', "") while source_id is also record.get("source_id", ""), losing the need record_id.
Job 2 input evidence_sources contains record_id values "s01" through "s08", while the needs and coverage record_id values are "n06-r01" through "n06-r08".
In job_2 prioritize, rank_by_record_id is keyed by evidence_sources.record_id and looked up with coverage.record_id, so the mismatch yields upstream_rank 0 for all observed priorities.
initial_receipt.explanation: The execution contains a provenance handoff fault. Job 1 produced evidence_sources whose record_id values are source IDs (s01..s08) rather than the selected need record IDs (n06-r01..n06-r08). Job 2 then cannot join provenance ranks back to coverage records by record_id, so every priority row has upstream_rank 0. The downstream output preserves the visible priority order by coincidence, but it does not preserve the upstream provenance identities/ranks required by the criteria.
